subject: Request: temporary TTFT and token/sec carveout for GraceTech pilot
messages:
From: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@gracetech.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: devops@gracetech.com
Date: 2026-09-03T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ask — TTFT / token/sec carveout request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the Redwood runtime looks promising. We're about to kick off a two-week external demo for a strategic customer (payment flows, low tolerance for truncation). Based on our internal load profile (attached CSV), we see very spiky streaming traffic: short bursts of high token emission interleaved with quiet periods.

Two items we need to formalize before the demo starts next week:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT): For the streaming endpoint to be usable in our UX we need a pragmatic TTFT target of <= 250 ms for 95% of requests during demo windows.
2) Token/sec expectations: We expect sustained per-connection emission of ~800 tokens/sec with burst headroom up to 3k tokens/sec for windows under 20s. We understand this exceeds Redwood's default public streaming profile; we're requesting a temporary carveout while we complete the pilot.

We can commit to a short-term reserved capacity increase if that is a hard requirement, but we need your legal/ops sign-off on a 60–90 day exception to avoid rollback mid-demo.

Attached: GraceTech_SLA_Exception_Request_v1.pdf (proposal) and token-velocity-sample.csv (5k rows).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Accept a temporary TTFT/token/sec exception for a bounded pilot?
- Provide telemetry hooks (per-request trace ids, token emission metrics) so we can run validation?

Appreciate a quick confirmation — demo prep is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Aisha Raman
Director, Platform Engineering
GraceTech Systems
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@gracetech.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-03T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — TTFT / token/sec carveout request

Aisha — thanks for the details and the CSV, that helps a lot. Short answer: we can usually accommodate pilot carveouts, but we need to lock down operational guardrails so we don't impact other customers. A few clarifying points and a proposed path forward: 

Questions:
- Is the 250 ms TTFT target for cold connections or warm sessions (i.e., with warmed KV cache)?
- For the 3k tokens/sec bursts, how frequent are those bursts and how many concurrent connections exhibit them in your sample?

Proposed path (we can iterate):
1) Run a short load test this Friday on a dedicated pilot pool (you run the client, we provide ephemeral credentials). We'll capture TTFT and tokens/sec traces.
2) If traces match your CSV, we provision a temporary policy: 60 days exception scoped to your pilot pool, with a token-rate policy that allows the burst headroom but includes a soft-fallback to the sync endpoint if backend backpressure occurs.
3) We will expose per-request tracing + a pre-defined metric dashboard (tokens/sec by connection, TTFT histogram) and require telemetry to be streamed to your monitoring during the pilot.
4) Legal: we'll attach a carveout addendum that limits exposure and includes SLA credits if we miss targets by >2x for a sustained window.

I’m looping in Laura (ops/partnerships) and Rishi (SLA/contracts) to scope the risk and craft the addendum. If you can confirm whether TTFT target is measured from an already-warmed session, we can prioritize kernel & cache tuning on the pilot pool.

I’ll schedule a 30-min runbook call with your DevOps and our SRE to run the Friday test. Proposed times: Fri 09:00 or 13:00 PT. Which works?

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-03T19:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — TTFT / token/sec carveout request

Markus / Rishi — quick internal note on negotiation posture and risk controls.

Context (short): GraceTech wants 250 ms TTFT (95%) + sustained 800 t/s per connection and bursts to 3k t/s. These are above our public streaming defaults but not outside what a dedicated pilot pool can deliver if we: (a) provision capacity, (b) enable pre-warmed KV caches, and (c) apply temporary throttles & circuit-breakers.

Recommended compromise to protect platform and revenue: 
- Offer a 60-day carveout (not 90) contingent on:
  * Commitment to a minimum reserved capacity (specify N GPUs based on Friday's test).
  * Telemetry enabled (trace-ids + Prom counters forwarded to both parties).
  * An automatic downgrade path: if error rate or tail-queueing exceeds thresholds for >2m, traffic is routed to a sync fallback and the carveout pauses.
- SLA language: carveout addendum should be explicit that TTFT target applies only to \"pilot pool instances\" and that unit cost adjustments apply for sustained >75% utilization. Include a clause for an audit of telemetry logs at Redwood's discretion.
- Credits: If we miss TTFT by >2x for >5 consecutive minutes during a demo window, credit 10% of that window's usage up to a cap.

Operational items for Friday test:
- Rishi: can you prepare a short addendum template and note typical quantized thresholds we can offer?
- Markus: schedule the SRE runbook with GraceTech. I'll prepare the dashboard and a quick runbook snippet for the DevOps team.

Attachment: proposed-carveout-language.txt (draft) [stub].

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@gracetech.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: devops@gracetech.com
Date: 2026-09-04T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — TTFT / token/sec carveout request

Markus / Laura — thanks, that approach sounds reasonable and pragmatic. A few confirmations from our side:

- The 250 ms TTFT target is for warm sessions (we can do a warm-up sequence in the client prior to the demo window).
- Bursts to 3k t/s are infrequent (~3% of requests) and typically not concurrent across many users — most bursts are single-connection.
- We can commit to a 60-day carveout rather than 90 if we increase reserved capacity during the demo window.

We’re available for the Friday 09:00 PT run (please send invite). We'll bring our SRE lead and an automated runner that can produce the trace ids you want in advance.

Thanks — attaching a short runbook and our demo window schedule.

Best,
Aisha Raman
Director, Platform Engineering
GraceTech Systems
Attachment stubs: GraceTech_SLA_Exception_Request_v1.pdf (PDF), token-velocity-sample.csv (CSV)
